policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: ASV 'to speak for thyself' renders either preposition; hyper and peri with the reflexive are both 'for/concerning thyself' in English.
Pure transposition. ASV renders both the participial phrase and the finite verb ('stretched forth his hand, and made his defence'); English order is the translator's, not the Greek's.
Pure transposition of 'this day' against the infinitive; ASV 'to make my defence before thee this day' renders both elements under either order.

ASV 'customs' sits within the range of both ethon and ethon (manners/customs); no English reflex separates them. The verse note is alternative_rendering (placement of 'especially') and does not bear on the reading.
ASV 'I beseech thee' supplies an object that English idiom requires after 'beseech' whether or not sou stands in the Greek; the render shows no italic supply to settle it.
Article before the attributive phrase; 'which was from the beginning' reflects the phrase itself, and English shows no trace of the article either way.
Connective te; ASV 'My manner of life then from my youth up' carries no 'both...and' pairing or other reflex that would require it.
ASV 'all the Jews' is the ordinary rendering of pantes Ioudaioi as well as pantes hoi Ioudaioi; the English article does not report the Greek one.
ASV 'made of God unto our fathers' renders eis and pros alike as 'unto'.
ASV reads 'unto our fathers'; the possessive 'our' renders hemon, which r01 omits.
ASV 'I am accused by the Jews, O king!' has no 'Agrippa', so r02 is excluded. r00-base and r01 differ only in the punctuation before the vocative, which the ASV's own pointing does not report.
ASV 'I both shut up many of the saints in prisons... and when they were put to death I gave my vote' renders the correlative te with 'both'; r01 omits it and leaves nothing for 'both'.
ASV 'in prisons' renders the plain dative as readily as en with the dative.
ASV 'Whereupon as I journeyed' shows no adjunctive 'also', but an unrendered kai is equally consistent with that; the verse note is alternative_rendering.
ASV reads 'the authority and commission of the chief priests' — a genitive relation. The same ASV chapter renders para as 'from the chief priests' (26:10); r01's para would give 'from', not 'of'.
ASV 'And when we were all fallen to the earth' renders te and de alike as 'and'.

ASV has the single participle 'saying', the ASV equivalent of legousan; lalousan is rendered 'speaking' in the ASV, and in r01 it stands with a second participle ('and saying') that the English does not show.
ASV has one participle of speaking only, 'a voice saying unto me'; r01's added kai legousan would give a second 'and saying' with no counterpart in the English.
ASV reads 'And the Lord said, I am Jesus'; the named subject renders kyrios, which r01 omits (leaving 'And he said').

ASV text reads 'the things wherein thou hast seen me', rendering me; the mapped textual_variant note ('Many ancient authorities read which thou hast seen') records the me-less reading as the alternative, not the text.
ASV 'delivering thee from the people' renders exairoumenos with the genitive with or without ek.
Pure transposition of verb and pronoun; ASV 'unto whom I send thee' is the same under either order.

ASV reads 'that they may turn from darkness to light', the ASV rendering of epistrepho; hypostrepsai would give 'return', which the English does not have. The verse note is alternative_rendering (transitive 'to turn them') and does not bear on the reading.
ASV 'declared both to them of Damascus first, and at Jerusalem' renders the correlative te...kai with 'both...and'; r01 omits te.
ASV 'throughout all the country of Judaea' fits the bare accusative of extent and is not excluded by eis; the English preposition does not report which Greek construction stood.
Finite verb against participle. ASV 'but declared' is the ordinary English handling of a Greek circumstantial participle as well as of a finite imperfect, so the English does not report which stood.
Transposition with an article; ASV 'the Jews seized me in the temple' renders anarthrous Ioudaioi as 'the Jews' too, and English order is the translator's.
ASV 'seized me in the temple' absorbs a copular participle onta ('me being in the temple') without a distinct word, so the English does not report its presence.
ASV 'the help that is from God' renders apo and para alike as 'from'.
ASV 'should proclaim light both to the people and to the Gentiles' renders the correlative te...kai with 'both...and'; r01 omits te.
ASV reads 'Festus saith with a loud voice' — a present tense rendering phesin; r01's ephe is past and the ASV renders such forms 'said'.
ASV reads 'But Paul saith'; the named subject renders Paulos, which r01 omits (leaving 'But he saith').
ASV reads 'unto whom also I speak freely'; the adjunctive 'also' renders kai, which r01 omits.
ASV 'none of these things is hidden from him' shows no separate word for the indefinite ti, which English absorbs into the negative pronoun either way.
Orthographic variation of the same word (outhen/ouden); ASV 'none of these things' is identical under either.
Periphrastic against simple form; ASV 'for this hath not been done in a corner' is the same English under either, and the copula has no separate reflex.

ASV 'And Agrippa said unto Paul' has a verb of speaking, but the base reading's ellipsis obliges the translator to supply one; the render carries no italic marking, so the English does not report whether ephe stood.
ASV reads 'thou wouldest fain make me a Christian' — a transitive 'make' rendering poiesai; r01's genesthai is intransitive 'become' and would give 'that I become a Christian'.

ASV 'And Paul said' has a verb of speaking, but the base reading's ellipsis obliges the translator to supply one; the render carries no italic marking, so the English does not report whether eipen stood.
ASV text reads 'with much', which suits pollo literally and megalo in its quantitative sense; the note offering 'in great' is classed alternative_rendering and cannot decide the reading.
ASV begins 'And the king rose up' with no rendering of r01's added genitive absolute 'And when he had said these things'.
ASV 'the king rose up, and the governor, and Bernice' joins the subjects with plain 'and'; te left unrendered in a simple list is not excluded by that.
Pure transposition of axion; English idiom requires 'worthy' before both genitives ('nothing worthy of death or of bonds') under either Greek order.
ASV 'This man doeth nothing worthy of death' shows no separate reflex of the indefinite ti alongside ouden.
